clue.text: Giving lecture, do numbers that prime divides

indicators.note: A thing that divides comes down in the middle of what it lands on, so the piece named before it splits open and the other one sits in the gap.

parts.note: a performer does numbers on stage, the numbers being the songs in the set
an athlete in their prime is at their peak

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is dressed up as arithmetic, and none of it is maths: the numbers are songs and the prime is a high point of form.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving lecture -> SPEAKING: the sense of the word that means addressing an audience from a platform, not merely talking to somebody.

clue.text: Very desirable bachelor perfectly erect

parts.note: a plum job or a plum role is the one everybody wants
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a personal ad, and the answer belongs on a building site: nothing about the man survives into the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: perfectly erect -> PLUMB: a builder's plumb line hangs true from a lead weight, so plumb means exactly vertical rather than just upright.

clue.text: Every guy in first set of books back for novelist's growing plot

indicators.note: the books abbreviation sits in among the words for every guy, splitting them

parts.note: every guy is all men
OT, the Old Testament, is the first set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of novelist

parts.note: the final letter of novelist

explanation.surface: Every man in some early books leaves the plot to grow for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: OT goes in between ALL and MEN, then 'back for' adds the last letter of novelist. An allotment is a rented patch of land in Britain where people grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small rented patch of ground for cultivating vegetables and flowers.

clue.text: Islands that are East or West, mostly free from big business

indicators.note: Mostly a word is nearly all of it, which in a crossword means everything except the letter at the end - here a final S.

parts.words: Islands that are East or West
parts.note: one group of these islands lies east and the other west, and both go by the same six-letter plural, which is one letter too long

explanation.walkthrough: East and West both point at the same six letters, which is the whole joke of the surface. The answer is short for independent.
explanation.definitionFit: free from big business -> INDIE: a label, band or film made outside the major corporations is called indie, the trade word for working unbacked.

clue.text: Wild fruit tree in western state present to the north

parts.note: Goa is a state on the west coast of India

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to the north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a gift is a present

explanation.surface: A wild fig tree grows in a state in the west, a gift to the region further north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' writes GIFT upwards, TFIG, beneath GOA. 'western state' looks American, but it is the Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat fig is the wild form of the common fig, also called the caprifig, used to pollinate cultivated figs.

clue.text: Get ready for a night out?

definitions.meaning: the setter means a night spent outdoors under canvas, and preparing for one means pitching the tents before dark
the surface sells an evening in town, dinner and a show, the sort of night you dress up for

explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay to pick apart here: the whole clue is one definition, and all of the work is in which kind of night out is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Get ready for a night out? -> ENCAMP: to encamp is to pitch a tent and settle in, so preparing for a night outdoors is the whole of it.

clue.text: Living arrangement snug during English spring

indicators.note: What happens during something else falls inside it rather than before or after, so the word just clued is planted in the middle.

parts.note: E is the usual single-letter abbreviation for English
to spring from something is to stem from it, both meaning to originate there
a snug room and a cosy one are the same warm idea

explanation.walkthrough: 'English spring' looks like weather, and 'spring' is a verb here, the one hiding in 'stems from'. The arrangement is a community of organisms, not a flatshare.
explanation.definitionFit: Living arrangement -> ECOSYSTEM: the plants, animals and habitat of a place taken as one working unit, which is how living things arrange themselves.

clue.text: Organised action saving North American mammal

indicators.note: Something being organised is being put into an order it did not have, so the letters handed over are free to be rearranged.
Saving here means excepting, the sense in 'all saving one', so the letter named next is held back from the mix.

parts.note: action supplies the letters, minus the one the next word holds back
N is the compass abbreviation for north, and this is the letter that never makes it in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving North' reads as a rescue mission and is a subtraction, and 'Organised action' as a well-run campaign. Neither phrase means what the surface says.
explanation.definitionFit: American mammal -> COATI: a long-snouted, ring-tailed relative of the raccoon from the New World tropics, placed here by continent alone.

clue.text: Road sign, in case you should have motorway ahead

indicators.note: Whatever is ahead of the rest goes in front, so the piece named beside it opens the answer instead of trailing at the end.

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's oldest long-distance motorway, and its number doubles as a letter
lest means in case something bad happens, as in 'lest we forget'
the formal impersonal pronoun stands in for you: one does not do that sort of thing

explanation.walkthrough: The motorway gets in by shape rather than by sound, the digit borrowed as a capital I. Milestones were the original road signs, cut stones counting down to the next town.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sign -> MILESTONE: a marker set at the roadside telling travellers how far they have come, which is a sign by a road doing its job.

clue.text: Mathematician's prompt returning cap

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for prompt is read from right to left

parts.note: a cue is a prompt, as given to an actor
a lid is a cap or cover

explanation.surface: A mathematician is prompted to give back a borrowed cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay. 'returning' acts only on the prompt, not the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer whose Elements was the standard textbook of mathematics for two millennia.

clue.text: Mother returned by 1 without thinking what might be wrong

definitions.text: without thinking what might be wrong

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for mother is read backwards

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
the answer to 1 across means giving a lecture, and doing so means communicating by voice, that is orally

explanation.surface: A mother answers back in speech without stopping to consider if she is in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes AM from MA; 1 across is SPEAKING, and something done by speaking is done ORALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To act amorally is to act with no regard for morality at all, unconcerned with right and wrong.

clue.text: Several quick strokes of the lash as foreplay?

definitions.meaning: the setter means an eyelash instead, fluttered rapidly against a partner's cheek, which is why they come several at a time
the surface reading is a whipping, in which a lash is a whip and the strokes are blows

explanation.walkthrough: No letters change hands anywhere in this one: the whole clue is the definition, and the only job is working out which sort of lash is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluttering your eyelashes against someone's skin is a butterfly kiss, named for the beating wings, so the lash is an eyelash and the strokes are the flutter.

clue.text: Eccentric freak caught by mean spook

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are caught, held inside, the word for mean

parts.note: tight means stingy, mean with money

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of freak are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A weirdo is grabbed by a nasty ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of FREAK, made by 'Eccentric', goes inside TIGHT, as 'caught by' shows. Spook here is the verb, as a horse spooks.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook, said of a horse or person, is to become suddenly frightened and startled.

clue.text: Peace — Crimea's flourishing with it

indicators.note: To flourish something is to wave it about, and letters waved about like that do not settle back in the order they were given.

parts.note: seven letters, the S of the apostrophe included, all of them fodder
two more letters join the pile before the shuffle

explanation.walkthrough: The dash after the first word is standing in for an equals sign, and the Crimean War is a red herring: Crimea is here only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace -> ARMISTICE: an agreed halt to the shooting, the truce signed while a treaty is still being negotiated, so peace in its narrow military sense.

clue.text: Meat curry, good parts horse rib

indicators.note: To part two things is to come between them, so the letter named beforehand pushes into the middle of the word that follows.

parts.note: a roan is a horse with white hairs mixed through its coat
G is the standard abbreviation for good, as on a school report
to rib someone is to josh them, teasing without malice

explanation.walkthrough: The dish is a Kashmiri lamb curry, red from mild chillies rather than heat. 'Good parts horse rib' is a butcher's window and no part of the recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat curry -> ROGAN JOSH: a slow-cooked lamb dish from Kashmir in a deep red sauce, so the definition gives the category and leaves the animal to you.

clue.text: Bit of tooth decay multiplied internally

indicators.note: Multiplying makes more of a thing, and doing it internally means the letter standing in the middle of the word gets written twice.

parts.note: a tooth or a fence post left to decay will rot
the middle letter of that three-letter word turns up a second time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tooth decay' offers itself as a single idea and the clue wants the two words prised apart, one for the definition and one for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit of tooth -> ROOT: the part below the gumline that anchors a tooth in the jaw, which is what a dentist means by a root canal.

clue.text: Charlie finished cutting grass, green again after drought?

indicators.note: Cutting into something goes through the middle of it with a blade, so the letters just assembled slice into the word that follows.

parts.note: a reed is the tall grass that grows in wet ground, and it opens after two letters
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet, alongside Alpha and Bravo
when a match is finished it is over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is the radio alphabet rather than a man, and 'cutting grass' sounds like mowing the lawn, which is the very picture the definition is painting.
explanation.definitionFit: green again after drought -> RECOVERED: a lawn burnt brown and then come back is said to have recovered, the word used of anything returning to health.

clue.text: Let out on reversal of prison sentence

indicators.note: a reversal turns something round, so the word for a prison sentence is written backwards

parts.note: time is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released after a court overturns the sentence on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' suggests a released prisoner, but it means give off: TIME is turned round by 'reversal of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or discharge, as a sound, light or gas is let out.

clue.text: In shock, return edition full of nasty sex

indicators.note: A thing full of something has it inside, so the pair of letters named at the end goes within what has been built already.

parts.note: to return somewhere is to go back there, two short words run together
ED is the standard abbreviation for edition, as on a title page
SM is the usual shorthand for sadomasochism

explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like an instruction to reverse something and is only a word to translate. Being gobsmacked is being struck in the gob, the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: In shock -> GOBSMACKED: utterly astonished, as though somebody had slapped you in the mouth, the British slang for the moment speech fails you.

clue.text: GP's location that's unsatisfactory and wet

parts.note: the noise of contempt you make when something is no good, the one Scrooge is famous for
what makes a day a wet one

explanation.walkthrough: 'GP' sends you straight to a doctor's surgery, and the surface keeps you there with a grumble about the weather. The capital letters are the tell.
explanation.definitionFit: GP's location -> BAHRAIN: this small Gulf island state hosts a round of the Formula One world championship, so a Grand Prix is held there each year.

clue.text: Small flat subsequently hosts have converted, a delightful place

indicators.note: A host takes guests into the house, so the word doing the hosting opens up and keeps the other letters inside it.

parts.note: S is the clothing-label abbreviation for small

indicators.note: Converting turns a thing into something else made of the same stuff, which for four letters means the same four in a different arrangement.

parts.note: a flat surface is an even one, level all the way across
what happens subsequently happens then, and the word splits after two letters
the four letters of have, rearranged before they move in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Small flat' is an estate agent's phrase and the two words are clued separately. The place itself is the topmost of the seven heavens, the one nearest God.
explanation.definitionFit: a delightful place -> SEVENTH HEAVEN: the phrase names a state of perfect happiness, which the definition treats as somewhere a person can be in.

clue.text: Landscape remains in a box upside-down

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the remains word goes into the other letters
in a down entry, upside-down means the letters are read from the bottom up, so in reverse

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, abbreviated TV
remains means is, continues to be, as in it remains open

explanation.surface: A landscape painting is still stored upside-down in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' suggests a crate, but in Britain the box is slang for television. 'upside-down' flips 'a box' as a whole, and only then does 'in' insert the remains word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a broad view of scenery, the sweep of countryside one sees from a high point.

clue.text: Provide means of support for heel that hurts

parts.note: the heel of a loaf is the crusty end of it
the two letters you shout when something stings

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about a shoe, and neither half of the wordplay is about feet: one is bread and the other is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Provide means of support -> ENDOW: to endow a university chair or a hospital bed is to settle money on it so it keeps going unaided.

clue.text: Silly hotel apparently competing with the Plaza?

definitions.note: The definition is an adjective and the answer is a person - the setter is letting the quality stand for whoever has it, the way 'you big silly' does.

parts.note: the Plaza is the grand hotel on Central Park, so a rival to it stands in New York, whose two letters go round the outside
a small hotel is an inn

explanation.walkthrough: No word here says 'inside': the geography does it, because a hotel taking on the Plaza has to be in the same city.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly -> NINNY: a ninny is a foolish, feeble creature, the mild playground insult for someone behaving daftly rather than someone genuinely stupid.

clue.text: People scattered seeing snake interrupt radio broadcast

indicators.note: the snake breaks into the middle of the rearranged letters, interrupting them
broadcast in its old sense of scattered widely, so the letters of radio are scattered

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Listeners hear of a snake disrupting a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests the radio itself, but it signals an anagram of RADIO, and ASP goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a population dispersed far from its homeland, like the Jewish diaspora.

clue.text: Bold sound of operatic cycle in German

indicators.note: sound of means we need a word that is said the same way as the German phrase

parts.note: Wagner's operatic cycle is the Ring, called Der Ring des Nibelungen in German, so the Ring is Der Ring

explanation.surface: A bold sound comes from Wagner's opera cycle, sung in German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of' asks for a homophone: Der Ring, German for the Ring, is pronounced much like the English adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring means adventurous and willing to take risks, which is what a bold person is.

clue.text: Claire has homework including AI's thoughts on topic?

definitions.note: The definition is a plural phrase and the answer a singular noun: the setter means everything a machine produces on a subject, taken together as one warmed-up lump.

indicators.note: Including means the words on either side are carrying something within them, so the letters wanted are already written out in order.

parts.note: six letters in a row, beginning inside the name and stopping just inside the last word

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the joke: what a chatbot hands you is old material warmed up. Nothing has to be built, because the letters are already sitting in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: AI's thoughts on topic -> REHASH: a rehash is old material served again with a fresh surface, which is what a machine trained on other people's writing returns.

clue.text: A lack of banknotes, say, circulating currently

indicators.note: Something circulating is going round and round, and letters sent round like that do not come back in the order they set off in.

parts.note: a lack of something is no something at all
a thick fold of banknotes is a wad of them
the three letters of say, tumbled into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: Banknotes circulating is the surface picture, and the word actually being circulated is the little one you would skate past: 'say' is fodder, not the usual for-example marker.
explanation.definitionFit: currently -> NOWADAYS: in the present age, the stretch of years we are living through, rather than at this exact moment.
